scope: Single and multiple URL UI parsing, D-054 / R-026 / FR-028 / AC-011 / T21
provenance: Actual local validation of the uncommitted single/batch UI follow-up; prior single-URL evidence is preserved in ui-validation.json

tests.skip_reason: Remote integration requires explicit authorization and configured real resources
tests.browser: Existing Microsoft Edge, headless, isolated fresh contexts
tests.network: Ephemeral loopback API, temporary SQLite/content, synthetic results only
verified: Original single-URL admission, extraction, body, download, auth, cancel, resume, reset, keyboard and Unicode tests still pass
Explicit Multiple URLs and Single URL modes both submit via the existing API
Whitespace/newline/tab-separated URL parsing preserves query commas
Duplicate URLs share one result row/job
Three distinct jobs retain two successes and one blocked outcome
Selecting different successes retrieves each exact job body
A body response arriving after row selection changes is ignored
Selecting a blocked result hides successful content and reports HTTP status
Batch JSON includes all observed job outcomes and excludes the API key
Canceling one selected batch job leaves its sibling queued
More than 100 URLs, non-HTTP(S) URLs and UTF-8 payloads above 64 KiB are rejected before admission
Switching back to single mode ignores hidden batch validation state
Batch result layout has no horizontal document overflow at a 390 by 844 viewport

packaging.smoke: Verified exact source bytes for all three assets, extracted wheel, asserted import origin, served HTML/CSS/JS and confirmed unauthenticated job read returns 401

behavior.batch_polling: One unfinished job per poll, at least 1500 ms between completed automatic polls
behavior.download_scope: Selected result or current entire-batch snapshot

limitations: No deployment, commit, push or cloud spending
No new public-site crawl or load test
100 unfinished jobs can take roughly 150 seconds plus API latency for a full status refresh
Shared API quota still applies to manual body/cancel actions and other clients
API remains authoritative for all URL restrictions and whole-batch acceptance
Batch UI does not replace streaming ingestion for large source datasets
Remote mandatory-engine, public demo and native-browser isolation gates remain open
Browser layout and keyboard checks are not an independent accessibility audit
